title: Skids & ABS
whatItIs: A skid happens when the tyres lose grip. ABS helps you keep steering control, but don't assume it will stop you sooner.
keyFacts: Skids are usually caused by harsh braking, accelerating or steering, or by going too fast for the conditions.
If the rear of the car skids to the right, steer immediately to the right to recover.
In a skid, remove the cause: release the brake pedal fully or ease off the accelerator.
With ABS, brake firmly in an emergency and keep your foot down: you can still steer.
Don't assume a car with ABS will stop in a shorter distance.

items.title: Rear skid
items.text: Release the brake or ease off the accelerator, and steer the same way as the skid.

items.title: ABS
items.text: Stops the wheels locking when you brake hard, so you can still steer.

items.title: Emergency stop (no ABS)
items.text: Brake immediately, but try not to lock the wheels: locked wheels can mean loss of control.

items.title: Speed still matters
items.text: Skids are often caused by driving too fast for the road conditions.

b.label: Without ABS
points: Harsh braking can lock the wheels
Locked wheels can cause loss of control

onTheTest.question: The rear of your car skids to the right. What should you do?
onTheTest.why: Release the brake or ease off the accelerator, and steer in the direction of the skid: if the rear skids right, steer right.

traps: Don't assume ABS will stop you in a shorter distance.
With ABS in an emergency, brake firmly and don't release until you have slowed down.
In a skid, release the brake pedal fully or ease off the accelerator.
